https://www.politico.eu/article/azerbaij.text: French citizen Martin Ryan is being released from Azerbaijani prison, one day after Paris successfully lobbied Brussels to lift sanctions on Russian billionaire Alisher Usmanov. Ryan, who was convicted of espionage charges, was the only French prisoner among several individuals pardoned by Azerbaijan President Ilham Aliyev on Wednesday. The Financial Times reported that the delisting was part of a deal that could see French nationals released from detention in Azerbaijan. Paris has significantly stepped up its role in the South Caucasus in support of Armenia, a pro-EU democracy that has spent decades locked in conflict with Azerbaijan. Advertisement Advertisement For more than a week, France held up the EU’s entire framework of individual sanctions in support of Ukraine with its surprise campaign to drop sanctions on Usmanov, who made his fortune in mining and telecoms. The French Ministry of Foreign Affairs said last week the push to delist Usmanov was a matter of national security, but the clash put at risk the expiry of the 3,000-odd listings if the EU’s 27 countries couldn’t agree to a deal to renew them. A deal was finally reached Tuesday. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha criticized the decision to delist Usmanov and banking magnate Mikhail Fridman, calling it “shameful and unjustifiable.” But French European Affairs Minister Benjamin Haddad called Tuesday’s outcome a win for European solidarity. “We keep a very strong united front on the sanctions on Russia,” Haddad told POLITICO. “We have these discussions. You have consideration of national security and others among member states. But the most important is that we’ve shown once again our unity and our resolve to put economic pressure on Russia for its war of aggression.” This developing story has been updated. https://www.dailystar.co.uk/news/world-n.text: A terrifying alert that Putin may be plotting to strike the UK has been issued as NATO is put on high alert. Poland's Prime Minister disclosed on Thursday evening that Russia is preparing to unleash missile attacks on nations backing Ukraine . Donald Tusk delivered the warning of broader warfare after the country was compelled to shut its airspace and airports due to the Kremlin's assault. He confirmed to parliament that Western intelligence services have authenticated Putin's schemes to launch additional attacks. Britain is expected to be amongst the nations Russia intends to target as a crucial supporter of Ukraine, the Mail reports. Mark Rutte, NATO chief, stated that the UK requires a 'credible path' towards reaching its defence spending target with 'yearly increments'. Should Russia launch missile attacks on British installations this would mark a dramatic escalation of hostilities. Russian drone assaults and surveillance operations within NATO airspace have happened previously but not missile attacks. The air assault in Poland occurred merely days after a railway station near the border was almost hit by a high-speed jet-powered drone with Western officials including former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson aboard. Tusk informed Polish MPs: "We know he is plotting something bad. However, for us the most important task is to prepare for various scenarios. "We will certainly not naively accept such messages that Russia has goodwill and will start behaving properly. There is no indication of this." Tusk went on to say that intelligence was 'very consistent and convincing' and cautioned that Russia might present future strikes as accidental. He further stated that Russia is seeking to challenge NATO's determination like never before in the months ahead. As Russia escalates their deployment of jet-powered drones across western Ukraine, there have been appeals for Britain and other partners to destroy them before they enter NATO airspace. Ben Wallace, former UK Defence Secretary characterised the action as 'the next natural step'. Tusk continued: "There is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles could penetrate the territory of one or more countries on the eastern flank and even cause damage, while the official explanation will be that there was an accident."

https://english.radio.cz/senate-speaker-.text: CS DE EN ES FR РУ УК Senate speaker invites Babiš to attend upper house sessions Facebook Twitter Czech Senate Speaker Miloš Vystrčil wants Prime Minister Andrej Babiš to start attending Senate sessions. He plans to invite him to the upper house’s inaugural session on November 19, following this year’s Senate elections. Vystrčil criticised Babiš for claiming last week that the Senate was pursuing an anti-Babiš agenda. He argued that the upper house was simply fulfilling its constitutional role, noting that it had returned only around 20 of some 150 bills to the Chamber of Deputies during its last term. In seven cases, MPs accepted the Senate’s proposed changes. The ANO party failed to win a single Senate seat in this year’s elections, despite 13 of its candidates reaching the run-off round. Babiš called the result “catastrophic” and said the party needed to examine the work of its regional organisations.
